I like your integration of the coop and the run as a single build. Did you put the base (landscape timber?) directly on the ground? In building ours I set concrete bricks 2-3 inches built on top of that to delay wood rot.

Thanks! The timber is sitting on the hardware cloth and the ground. We used treated 4x4s - spiked them into the ground. The coop is just about a year and a half old at this point - I'll hope that we don't get warping/rot too heavily with the treated wood, but we'll see! 8-)

The nesting boxes are in the coop - I'll get some pictures posted at some point. We used plastic bins with a hole cut in the back for easy access to the eggs. The door is sometimes too small - especially when reloading sand into the coop yard. We will likely make a double door on our next build...

Industry Analysts Speculate On Nintendo's Future And Satoru Iwata's Possible Successor

If Nintendo wants to come back from this slump they've been in they need to keep Miyamoto out of the CEO position, and focus on their IP and the NX just as the article says. They need to make a competitive console for the regular gaming community. Nintendo's innovations were fun while they lasted, but they should have been put out to pasture on the transition to the Wii U. I really hope Nintendo figures it out and sticks around as a contender in the gaming arena for as long as possible, but they won't be able to do it if they keep relying on gimmicks.
I foresee Nintendo foregoing the home console market entirely; From everything I've read (sorry, I don't have sources ready), Japanese gamers are mostly mobile-centric.

I've read that somewhere too, but Japan is 4th in where the most money is spent on video games with America, Canada, and the UK in the top three spots (at least on one site I found it could be wrong). So while they may very well forego a home console in the future and go the route of Sega (a much more succesful Sega) if they could cater to both console gamers and create a whole branch just for mobile gaming (handhelds, phones, tablets, w/e) I believe Nintendo could dominate the gaming indusrty just like they used to. Whatever they choose to do though I'm still going to buy their games.

The 3ds is a beast of a system with a very well populated games library. The wii and wii u look like look like failures in this regard. I'm not talking sales numbers on the systems themselves, but the variety and quality of their games library. Yes the first party games are great but without the third party support you feel left out of the rest of the gaming community.

I really hope they find a way to maybe combine the two systems into one. for example a system you can take with you on the bus and road trips or whatever but still be able to connect to the tv for that big screen experience. Then add in their special brand of Nintendo magic to really innovate on the idea and make it special. Also leave it accessible enough for third party developers to make games for it.

Lastly, make it powerful. I do not mind spending a bit more money on a system that will still look good 5 years from now. Obviously the battery life is going to suffer for this and I'm OK with that.

Common Nintendo. This is an opportunity to create a new start out of this heart breaking tragedy.
